info.title: OMS Platform API
info.description:
Multi-vendor commerce OMS API.

**Conventions**
- Base path `/api/v1`. Breaking changes ship as `/api/v2`; additive changes stay in v1.
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`. Tenant is derived from the token, never from the request body.
- Success: `{ "success": true, "data": ..., "requestId": "..." }`. Lists add `meta: { limit, nextCursor, hasMore }`.
- Errors: `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message", "details" }, "requestId": "..." }`.
- Pagination: keyset (`?limit=25&cursor=...`). Sorting: `?sort=-createdAt,name`. Filtering: `?filter[status]=active`. Search: `?q=`.
- Retriable POSTs accept `Idempotency-Key` (required where documented).
- Every response carries `X-Request-Id` and `X-Correlation-Id`.

incoming.description: Ordered / in transit, not yet received

status.description: draft -> ready (validated) -> approved (merchant) -> pending (submitted) -> active | rejected | correction_required; unpublished = taken down

safetyBuffer.description: Units always held back from this channel

patch.description: Each top-level section is merged, so `{ "notifications": { "lowStock": false } }` keeps the other notification flags.

get.description: Cross-tenant directory with search (`q`), `filter[status]`, `sort` (createdAt, displayName) and keyset pagination.

patch.description: Platform admins only. Suspending a vendor blocks all of its users immediately (login and API access return TENANT_SUSPENDED).

post.summary: Register a vendor (business) and its first administrator
post.description: Creates the vendor (tenant), the first user with the Vendor Admin role and sends an e-mail verification link. The caller then signs in with POST /auth/login.

post.summary: Sign in
post.description: Returns a short-lived access token (JWT) and a single-use refresh token. Repeated failures lock the account for 15 minutes.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new token pair
post.description: Refresh tokens are rotated on every use. Presenting an already-used token revokes the whole session (theft detection).

post.summary: Sign out (end the current session)
Sign out of every device
Verify an e-mail address
Send a new verification e-mail
Request a password-reset e-mail
post.description: Always answers 202, whether or not the address belongs to an account (no account enumeration).

post.summary: Set a new password using a reset token
post.description: Single-use token. Signs the user out of every device.

post.summary: Change my password
post.description: Signs out every other session.

get.description: System roles assignable to members: Vendor Admin, Vendor Staff, Vendor Viewer (platform staff also see platform roles).

get.summary: List the members of my vendor
get.description: Search (`q`: name/e-mail), `filter[status]`, `filter[role]`, `sort` (createdAt, fullName, email), keyset pagination.

patch.summary: Change a member's role, status or name
patch.description: Members cannot change their own role/status, and a vendor always keeps at least one active Vendor Admin. Disabling a member signs them out everywhere.

delete.summary: Remove a member from my vendor
delete.description: Soft-deletes the user and ends all of their sessions.

post.summary: Invite someone to my vendor
post.description: Sends an e-mail with a single-use link valid for 7 days. Requires a verified e-mail address on the inviting account. Roles: vendor_admin, vendor_staff, vendor_viewer.

post.summary: Resend an invitation (new link, new 7-day window)
Accept an invitation and create my account
post.description: Public endpoint used by the link in the invitation e-mail. The e-mail address is taken from the invitation (and counts as verified). Sign in afterwards with POST /auth/login.

post.description: Creates the canonical, marketplace-neutral product. `productCode` and every variant `sku` are unique per vendor (409 otherwise). Activating (`status: "active"`) needs at least one active variant.

version.description: Optimistic lock: send the version you read

post.description: Each item succeeds or fails independently (partial success, HTTP 200): inspect `results`. `delete` additionally needs products:delete. For files with thousands of rows use the CSV import (POST /products/imports).

post.summary: Start a product CSV import (step 1: create the job)
post.description: Returns the job and how to upload the CSV. Columns: product_code, title, description, brand, manufacturer, country_of_origin, category_slug, hsn_code, gst_rate_bps, tags (pipe-separated), status, sku, barcode, option_values (k=v;k=v), currency, mrp_minor, selling_price_minor, cost_price_minor, tax_rate_bps, weight_grams, length_mm, width_mm, height_mm, variant_status. Rows are grouped by product_code; products and SKUs are upserted.

post.summary: Upload the CSV for an import job (step 2)
post.description: Raw `text/csv` body, max 5 MB.

post.summary: Start an uploaded import (step 3)
Export products to CSV (asynchronous)

get.summary: Get a job (status, stats, row errors)

post.summary: Register a product image / document / listing document and get upload instructions
post.description: Step 1 of 2. Validates type (jpeg, png, webp, gif, pdf, csv, xlsx, docx), size (images 10 MB, documents 25 MB) and extension, then returns where to send the bytes. The first image of a product becomes its primary image automatically.

purpose.description: Defaults from the type: images → product_image, others → product_document

get.summary: List a product's images and documents
get.description: Ordered by sortOrder. Includes short-lived download URLs.

post.summary: Upload the file bytes through the API (step 2, "api" strategy)
post.description: Send the raw file as the request body with `Content-Type` equal to the declared mimeType. The content is sniffed: a file that is not really what it claims is rejected. `?primary=true` makes an image the primary one.

post.summary: Confirm a direct (presigned) upload (step 2, "presigned" strategy)
post.description: Verifies what actually landed in object storage: size limit and content sniffing. Rejected files are deleted.

patch.summary: Reorder, rename or make an image primary

delete.description: Soft-deletes the record and removes the stored object.

get.description: Streams the stored bytes through the API (any storage provider). Images are served inline, everything else as an attachment, always with nosniff.

post.summary: Create a warehouse
post.description: The first warehouse becomes the default. Stock is held per warehouse in /inventory.

patch.description: Send `version` for optimistic concurrency. The default warehouse cannot be deactivated or unset; a warehouse with reserved stock cannot be deactivated.

delete.description: Only an empty, non-default warehouse. Use PATCH status=inactive to retire one that holds history.

get.description: onHand / reserved / available / incoming / damaged / returned. `filter[low]` = at or below the reorder level; `filter[out]` = nothing available.

get.summary: Stock of one variant across all warehouses

post.summary: Receive stock into a warehouse
post.description: Adds to on-hand (writes a `receive` movement). With `fromIncoming` it also clears the same quantity from the warehouse's incoming bucket.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional idempotency key: repeating the same key never moves stock twice

post.summary: Record stock that is on its way
post.description: Increases the `incoming` bucket (not sellable until received).

idempotencyKey.description: Optional idempotency key: repeating the same key never moves stock twice

post.summary: Adjust stock (delta) or record a stock count
post.description: Exactly one of `delta` (+/- units) or `setOnHand` (a physical count: the ledger records the DIFFERENCE). A `reason` is mandatory. Never goes below zero or below what is reserved.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional idempotency key: repeating the same key never moves stock twice

post.summary: Move stock to / from the damaged bucket

idempotencyKey.description: Optional idempotency key: repeating the same key never moves stock twice

post.summary: Receive a customer return
post.description: `hold` = quarantine in the returned bucket until inspected; `restock` = sellable immediately; `damaged` = write-off bucket. Resolve held returns with POST /inventory/returns/resolve.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional idempotency key: repeating the same key never moves stock twice

post.summary: Inspect held returns: restock or write off

idempotencyKey.description: Optional idempotency key: repeating the same key never moves stock twice

put.summary: Set the low-stock threshold of a variant in a warehouse

get.description: Every quantity change, newest first, with running balances. Page with `before=<last id>`.

get.summary: Verify stock equals the movement ledger
get.description: Recomputes every quantity from the ledger and lists mismatches. An empty `drift` means no stock was ever changed without a movement.
Created when an order is imported, committed when it is dispatched, released when it is cancelled.

post.summary: Create a stock transfer between warehouses (draft)
Ship a transfer
post.description: Stock leaves the source warehouse now and shows as `incoming` at the destination.

post.summary: Receive a transfer
post.description: Defaults to receiving everything that was shipped. Pass `items` for a partial receipt: the shortfall is written back to the source warehouse.

post.summary: Cancel a transfer
post.description: A draft is simply cancelled; an in-transit transfer returns the stock to the source warehouse.

post.summary: Create a marketplace account (connection placeholder)
post.description: A vendor can hold many accounts, across and within marketplaces. The account starts as `pending_authorization`; connect it with POST /marketplace-accounts/{id}/authorize. Use marketplace `mock` for the sandbox.

externalAccountId.description: Seller id, if already known; otherwise it is filled in when you authorize

get.summary: Get a marketplace account (token metadata only, never secrets)

patch.summary: Rename, configure, pause or resume an account

delete.description: Refused (409) while the account is connected: disconnect it first.

get.summary: Marketplace connectors and their capability matrix
get.description: Marketplaces are NOT uniform: check `enabledCapabilities` before offering a feature. `planned` connectors are declared but not callable yet; `mock` is the sandbox.

get.summary: Capability matrix of the account's marketplace

get.description: Returns the marketplace URL to send the seller to, plus a signed, 10-minute `state` to pass back with the returned code (CSRF protection).

post.summary: Connect the account (exchange a code, or submit credentials)
post.description: Validates the credentials with the marketplace BEFORE storing them, then stores them encrypted (AES-256-GCM). The response contains token metadata only. Sandbox: code `sandbox-code[:sellerId[:ttlSeconds]]` or credentials `{ sellerId, apiKey: "sandbox_..." }`. Requires a verified e-mail address.

code.description: Authorization code returned by the marketplace (redirect flow)

externalAccountId.description: Seller id returned with the authorization code, for marketplaces that send it separately (e.g. Amazon selling_partner_id)

credentials.description: Direct credentials for marketplaces that use API keys (sent once, stored encrypted, never returned)

post.summary: Reconnect an account whose authorization expired or was revoked
post.description: Same inputs as /authorize; replaces the stored credentials and counts as a rotation.

code.description: Authorization code returned by the marketplace (redirect flow)

externalAccountId.description: Seller id returned with the authorization code, for marketplaces that send it separately (e.g. Amazon selling_partner_id)

credentials.description: Direct credentials for marketplaces that use API keys (sent once, stored encrypted, never returned)

post.summary: Rotate (refresh) the access token now
post.description: Normally automatic (ahead of expiry and on auth failures); this forces it. Increments `authorization.rotationCount`.

post.summary: Check the connection now
post.description: Calls the marketplace with the stored credentials (refreshing them if needed) and updates connection status, last success and last failure. Marketplace problems are reported in the body (`ok: false`), not as HTTP errors.

post.summary: Test the connection end to end (read-only)
post.description: Runs harmless read-only calls against the marketplace with the stored credentials: credentials, seller profile, catalogue read, order read. Each step reports success, latency and a message; steps the marketplace does not support are skipped. Nothing is changed on the marketplace.

post.summary: Disconnect the account
post.description: Destroys the stored credentials (irreversible) and marks the account `revoked`. Reconnect later with /reconnect.

get.summary: Fetch the seller profile from the marketplace
get.description: Capability `account.fetchProfile`.

get.summary: Preview products that already exist on the marketplace (import products)
get.description: Capability `catalog.import`. Read-only, paged with `cursor`. Use it to match marketplace SKUs with your catalogue before creating listings.

post.summary: Start a listing: master variant -> marketplace account
post.description: Step 1 of the flow: Master Product -> Select Marketplace -> Category Mapping -> Attribute Mapping -> Validation -> Preview -> Merchant Approval -> Publish -> Track Status. Creates a `draft`; one listing per variant per account.

patch.summary: Edit a listing (category, price, attribute values, stock limits)
patch.description: Editing content resets validation and approval. A LIVE listing (active/pending) only accepts price, MRP and stock-limit changes; a price change is pushed to the marketplace automatically. Send `version` for optimistic concurrency.

delete.summary: Delete a listing that never reached the marketplace

post.summary: Validate against the marketplace category rules
post.description: Resolves attribute values (your explicit values, then mappings, then core-field hints, then variant options), loads the category requirements from the marketplace and reports `errors` (blockers) and `warnings`. A valid draft becomes `ready`. The requirements come from the marketplace, so the account must be connected.

attributeSources.description: Where each resolved value came from

get.summary: Preview exactly what will be sent to the marketplace
get.description: No network write. Returns the marketplace request (`endpoint`, `payload`), the validation result and whether the merchant approval still matches the current content (`approval.current`).

post.summary: Merchant approval
post.description: Re-validates and records that THIS content was approved (by hash). Any later change to the content invalidates the approval; publishing requires a current approval.

post.summary: Publish (submit) an approved listing
post.description: Asynchronous: returns 202 with the sync job. The job submits the listing, records the marketplace's answer (`pending`, `active`, `rejected`, `correction_required`) and schedules status tracking. Repeating the call for the same approval returns the same job.

post.summary: Take a listing down from the marketplace
post.description: Asynchronous (202). Needs the marketplace capability `listings.deactivate`.

post.summary: Check this listing's status on the marketplace now
post.description: Asynchronous (202).

get.description: Every time the sellable quantity was sent to the marketplace: what central stock had available, what was requested, and the outcome (succeeded / failed + reason).
Live lookup through the connector (capability `listings.categorySearch`, cached for a few minutes).

get.summary: What the marketplace category requires for a listing
Suggested attribute mappings for a marketplace category
get.description: For every requirement: the mapping you already saved, or a proposal (a core field, or a vendor attribute with the same name). Apply a proposal with PUT /attribute-mappings.

put.summary: Map one of your categories to a marketplace category
put.description: Upsert per (marketplace, category). New listings of products in that category pick the marketplace category up automatically.

put.summary: Map a marketplace attribute to a source
put.description: Per (marketplace, marketplace category, marketplace attribute). The source is a product/variant `core_field` (title, description, brand, barcode, sku, price, mrp, hsn_code, country_of_origin, weight_grams, manufacturer), one of your `attribute` definitions, or a `static` value. `valueMap` translates your value into the marketplace's allowed value (e.g. {"Navy":"Blue"}).

post.summary: Import the products that already exist on the marketplace
post.description: Asynchronous (202). Fetches the marketplace catalogue page by page and stores each product in NORMALISED form (never the marketplace's own DTO). Review them under /imported-products, then create master products or link them to existing variants. Resumable after a failure.

post.summary: Create a MASTER product from an imported marketplace product
post.description: Marketplace Product -> Normalised Product -> Master Product. Creates the product + variant, and a tracked listing (already live, no publish). `initialQuantity` seeds opening stock through the ledger; without it no stock is invented and the marketplace quantity is NOT overwritten with zero.

post.summary: Link an imported product to an existing master variant
Ignore an imported product

get.description: sellable = clamp( floor(available x allocation%) - buffer, 0, max ). Each marketplace gets its own number; nothing is "the same quantity everywhere".

put.description: Changing the policy recomputes and re-pushes every live listing of the account (one coalesced job).

post.summary: Recompute and push every live listing's quantity now
post.description: Asynchronous (202). Normally automatic (event-driven); use after a policy change, an outage, or to reconcile.

post.summary: Check the status of every pending listing on the account
post.description: Asynchronous (202). Normally scheduled; this runs it now.

get.description: Normalised orders from every connected marketplace. `q` matches order number, marketplace order id and customer name/e-mail. `filter[attention]=true` lists orders that need a human (unmapped SKU, short stock).
Orders placed in the window (default last 30 days) across ALL marketplaces: totals by normalised status and by marketplace, plus how many open orders need attention.

get.summary: Get an order with its items

get.description: Append-only history of every status change (and every marketplace report that was ignored), oldest first.

post.summary: Move an order to its next status
post.description: Allowed steps: new -> confirmed -> picking -> packed -> ready_to_dispatch -> dispatched -> in_transit -> delivered; cancel is possible until dispatch; returned after dispatch. Dispatching consumes the reserved stock, cancelling releases it. The marketplace is informed asynchronously where it accepts that status (see `statusUpdate`).

post.summary: Cancel an order
post.description: Allowed until the order is dispatched. Held stock is released; the marketplace is told where it supports cancellation.

post.summary: Hold stock for the lines that are still short
post.description: Re-runs the reservation for an order that arrived while stock was short (it is also done automatically when stock is received). Never oversells.

get.description: Our system -> connector -> marketplace: every status change we asked a marketplace to apply, with its outcome (requested / sent / successful / failed / retrying / skipped).

post.summary: Retry a failed status push
Import orders from the marketplace now
post.description: Asynchronous (202). Normally scheduled; this runs it now. Optional `since` re-reads orders changed after that time (e.g. to backfill). Importing is idempotent: orders already imported are not duplicated.

get.description: Every marketplace synchronisation run: order imports, inventory/price pushes, listing publishes and status checks, catalogue imports, order status pushes. Keyset-paginated, newest first.

get.summary: One sync job (status, attempts, progress, failure details)

get.description: Append-only, oldest first. Pass `after=<last id>` to page.

post.summary: Retry a failed / dead-lettered job
post.description: Resets the attempt budget and queues the job again. Only failed, dead_lettered, partially_failed and cancelled jobs can be retried. Runners are idempotent, so already-processed items are not duplicated.

post.summary: Cancel a queued / retrying job
Receive a marketplace notification (called by the marketplace)
post.description: Public endpoint, authenticated by a per-account HMAC signature over the RAW body (see GET /marketplace-accounts/{id}/webhook-config for the header). Valid events are stored once (duplicate deliveries are acknowledged and dropped) and processed asynchronously with retries; the response only confirms receipt.

status.description: received -> processing -> processed | failed (will retry) | dead_lettered (retry it manually); ignored = authentic but not actionable; rejected = bad signature

deliveries.description: How many times the marketplace delivered this event (> 1 = duplicates were dropped)

post.summary: Process a failed / dead-lettered event again
post.description: Asynchronous (202). Processing is idempotent: an order that was already imported is not duplicated.

get.summary: Webhook callback URL and signing scheme for an account
get.description: Register `callbackUrl` with the marketplace and sign deliveries with the secret from POST .../webhook-secret.

post.summary: Generate or rotate the webhook signing secret
post.description: The secret is returned ONCE and stored encrypted; it cannot be read back. Rotating invalidates the previous secret immediately: update the marketplace configuration first (or accept a short gap).

configured.description: Has a signing secret been generated?

secret.description: Shown once. Store it in the marketplace configuration now.

get.description: Who did what, when, from where. Append-only and tenant-scoped; secrets are never recorded. Keyset pagination.
